newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RBNZ says inflation not dead, must stay vigilant.
newsitem.headline: RBNZ says inflation not dead, must stay vigilant.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand said in a document published on Friday that inflation was not dead and it needed to remain vigilant.

"The booklet's key message is an acknowledgement that right now exporters are hurting, but also that in the long term price stability is of greater value to exporters than any short-term gains that would follow from tolerating 'a bit of inflation'," RBNZ Governor Don Brash said in a statement.
The booklet, "The impact of monetary policy on exporters", was released in connection with a conference of exporters which Brash addressed in Wellington on Thursday.
Brash said that historically, any advantage to exporters from devaluations was soon taken back by inflation.
"The idea that a low dollar permanently enriches exporters is incorrect, as is the idea that a high dollar permanently impoverishes them," the bank said.
It said the booklet outlined the long-term distortionary effects of inflation, along with the inflationary risks of any marked easing in fiscal policy.
